A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Athena research work. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and section relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Best-of-N, step-judgment, fine-tuning and ablation results, including Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a fine-tuning comparison in Appendix C.5 and Table 11.

M1.justification: The consistency filter, ORM initialization, negative up-sampling and response-ranking procedures are retained. The revised ORM formulation matches solution-level training already described in v1; it does not establish an implementation change. The completer-size revision concerns experimental configuration.

E1.justification: Evaluation tasks and named training sources are retained. However, v2 Section 2.4 newly specifies excluding proof problems. v1 does not establish whether its retained training data included proofs, so an actual change in training task coverage cannot be determined.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds fine-tuning using all responses without Athena-PRM selection as a comparator to ranked fine-tuning on 30k queries. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated weak completer for process-label generation changes from Qwen2.5-VL-7B in v1 Section 2.3 to Qwen2.5-VL-3B in v2 Section 2.4. Appendix C.5 also introduces a 30k-query fine-tuning control. The PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an ablation testing whether PRM response selection improves fine-tuning. Appendix C.1 adds a qualitative finding that using additional completers brings no significant improvement despite increased computation. Existing ablations and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging five runs for Best-of-N evaluation. v2 adds no seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical testing procedure; its additional qualitative use of 'significant' does not document a test.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds MathVista accuracies of 68.7 without PRM selection and 69.8 with selection on 30k queries. Its 71.4 full-data result already appears in Table 4. Existing table values are retained, while Appendix C.1 adds the negative finding for additional completers.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 and Equation 1 correct the formal ORM definition from r(x,y,y*) with input (x,y) to r(x,a) with the full solution a. The reference answer remains in the correctness label rather than the reward arguments. The remaining mathematical formulations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: consistency-filtered process labels, 5K-sample data efficiency, ORM initialization, negative up-sampling and Athena-based reasoning improvements. The headline numerical claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix B's specific limitations concerning clear-answer tasks, open-ended generation and heuristic step segmentation. Appendix C.5 adds an explanation for omitting ORM selection: ground-truth answers are available. The main interpretations of retained results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents proof-problem exclusion and the 150k-query full fine-tuning setting, revises the weak completer specification and adds a direct VLMEvalKit repository link. It removes the explanation that short steps or steps without mathematical symbols are merged.

R1.justification: Research positioning is retained when v1 Section 4 is matched to v2 Appendix B. Publication and title updates refer to existing cited works. NuminaMath's formal bibliography entry replaces its existing dataset-link citation rather than introducing a new research source.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained with limited wording edits and author-year citations. Existing training strategies receive their own subsection, related work moves to Appendix B, and the appendices are reorganized with an added LLM drafting disclosure.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template throughout, changing title and header styling, table scale and placement. Tables 3 and 4 now share a page, Tables 6 and 7 occupy a separate table-only page, and Table 11 is added. All six existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new fine-tuning control strengthens evidence for response selection, and Equation 1 better matches the described ORM training. However, v2 removes specific limitations and step-merging instructions, weakening transparency and reproducibility. The unexplained completer-size revision alongside retained results adds uncertainty. These benefits and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
